sanskrit: aṣṭāviṃśatirātraṃ vā māsaṃ vā nūnam antataḥ yat tad āsīn mahad yuddhaṃ tatra me sārathir hataḥ
english: Twenty-eight nights ago, or at most a month, there was that great battle in which my charioteer was slain.

sanskrit: sa labheyaṃ yadi tv anyaṃ hayayānavidaṃ naram tvarāvān adya yātvāhaṃ samucchritamahādhvajam
english: If only I could find another man skilled in driving horses, I would go today with all speed, my great banner raised high.

sanskrit: vigāhya tatparānīkaṃ gajavājirathākulam śastrapratāpanirvīryān kurūñ jitvānaye paśūn
english: Plunging into their army, crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, I would defeat the Kurus — stripped of valour by my weapons — and bring back the cattle.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ kṛpam droṇaṃ ca saha putreṇa maheṣvāsān samāgatān
english: Duryodhana, the son of Śāntanu, Karṇa the son of Vikartana, Kṛpa, Droṇa together with his son — all these great archers assembled —

sanskrit: vitrāsayitvā saṃgrāme dānavān iva vajrabhṛt anenaiva muhūrtena punaḥ pratyānaye paśūn
english: — I would terrify them in battle as the bearer of the thunderbolt terrifies the demons, and in this very hour bring the cattle back again.

sanskrit: śūnyam āsādya kuravaḥ prayānty ādāya godhanam kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ yad ahaṃ tatra nābhavam
english: The Kurus seized their opportunity when the land was empty of defenders and march off taking the cattle-wealth. What could I do, since I was not there?

sanskrit: paśyeyur adya me vīryaṃ kuravas te samāgatāḥ kiṃ nu pārtho 'rjunaḥ sākṣād ayam asmān prabādhate
english: Let those assembled Kurus witness my valor today — as if to say, 'Can this be Pārtha Arjuna himself who harasses us?'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ strīṣu bhāṣataḥ sma punaḥ punaḥ nāmarṣayata pāñcālī bībhatsoḥ parikīrtanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As he kept repeating these words again and again among the women, the Pāñcālī princess could not bear to hear Bībhatsu's name spoken thus.

sanskrit: athainam upasaṃgamya strīmadhyāt sā tapasvinī vrīḍamāneva śanakair idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then that distressed woman came forward from among the ladies and, as if shyly, spoke these words to him softly.

sanskrit: yo 'sau bṛhadvāraṇābho yuvā supriyadarśanaḥ bṛhannaḍeti vikhyātaḥ pārthasyāsīt sa sārathiḥ
english: "That youth of mighty elephant-like splendor, handsome and delightful to behold, known by the name Bṛhannaḍā — he was the charioteer of Pārtha.

sanskrit: dhanuṣy anavaraś cāsīt tasya śiṣyo mahātmanaḥ dṛṣṭapūrvo mayā vīra carantyā pāṇḍavān prati
english: He was also second to none in archery, a pupil of that great soul. I saw him before, O hero, when I was moving among the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yadā tat pāvako dāvam adahat khāṇḍavaṃ mahat arjunasya tadānena saṃgṛhītā hayottamāḥ
english: When the fire burned that great forest of Khāṇḍava, it was he who controlled the excellent horses for Arjuna at that time.

sanskrit: tena sārathinā pārthaḥ sarvabhūtāni sarvaśaḥ ajayat khāṇḍavaprasthe na hi yantāsti tādṛśaḥ
english: With that charioteer, Pārtha conquered all creatures on every side at Khāṇḍavaprastha — for there is no driver like him.

sanskrit: yeyaṃ kumārī suśroṇī bhaginī te yavīyasī asyāḥ sa vacanaṃ vīra kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: This beautiful-hipped princess, your younger sister — he will do whatever she says, O hero; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi vai sārathiḥ sa syāt kurūn sarvān asaṃśayam jitvā gāś ca samādāya dhruvam āgamanaṃ bhavet
english: If he were to serve as charioteer, then without any doubt you would conquer all the Kurus, recover the cattle and certainly return home."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa sairandhryā bhaginīṃ pratyabhāṣata gaccha tvam anavadyāṅgi tām ānaya bṛhannaḍām
english: Thus addressed by the Sairandhrī, he spoke to his sister: "Go, O blameless-limbed one, and bring Bṛhannaḍā to me."

sanskrit: sā bhrātrā preṣitā śīghram agacchan nartanāgṛham yatrāste sa mahābāhuś channaḥ satreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Sent by her brother, she went quickly to the dance-hall where that mighty-armed Pāṇḍava dwelt, living in disguise.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā viśālākṣīṃ rājaputrīṃ sakhīṃ sakhā prahasann abravīd rājan kutrāgamanam ity uta
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing that wide-eyed princess, his companion addressed his companion with a laugh: "Where have you come from, O princess?"

sanskrit: tam abravīd rājaputrī samupetya nararṣabham praṇayaṃ bhāvayantī sma sakhīmadhya idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The princess approached that bull among men and, cultivating intimacy, spoke these words in the midst of the women companions:

sanskrit: gāvo rāṣṭrasya kurubhiḥ kālyante no bṛhannaḍe tān vijetuṃ mama bhrātā prayāsyati dhanurdharaḥ
english: "The cattle of the kingdom are being driven off by the Kurus, O Bṛhannaḍā. My brother, the bowman, is going to set out to defeat them.

sanskrit: naciraṃ ca hatas tasya saṃgrāme rathasārathiḥ tena nāsti samaḥ sūto yo 'sya sārathyam ācaret
english: Not long ago his charioteer was killed in battle, and there is no driver equal to him who could now serve as his charioteer.

sanskrit: tasmai prayatamānāya sārathyarthaṃ bṛhannaḍe ācacakṣe hayajñāne sairandhrī kauśalaṃ tava
english: For him who is thus seeking a charioteer, O Bṛhannaḍā, the Sairandhrī spoke of your skill in horse-lore.

sanskrit: sā sārathyaṃ mama bhrātuḥ kuru sādhu bṛhannaḍe purā dūrataraṃ gāvo hriyante kurubhir hi naḥ
english: Do serve well as charioteer for my brother, O Bṛhannaḍā — for the Kurus are already driving our cattle far away.

sanskrit: athaitad vacanaṃ me 'dya niyuktā na kariṣyasi praṇayād ucyamānā tvaṃ parityakṣyāmi jīvitam
english: If today, being urged out of affection, you will not do this thing I ask, I shall abandon my life."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu suśroṇyā tayā sakhyā paraṃtapaḥ jagāma rājaputrasya sakāśam amitaujasaḥ
english: Thus addressed by that beautiful-hipped companion, the scorcher of foes went to the presence of the prince of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: taṃ sā vrajantaṃ tvaritaṃ prabhinnam iva kuñjaram anvagacchad viśālākṣī śiśur gajavadhūr iva
english: She of wide eyes followed behind him as he walked quickly, like a young elephant-cow following behind a great maddened elephant.

sanskrit: dūrād eva tu taṃ prekṣya rājaputro 'bhyabhāṣata tvayā sārathinā pārthaḥ khāṇḍave 'gnim atarpayat
english: Seeing him from a distance, the prince spoke to him: "With you as charioteer, Pārtha satisfied the fire in the Khāṇḍava forest.

sanskrit: pṛthivīm ajayat kṛtsnāṃ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ sairandhrī tvāṃ samācaṣṭa sā hi jānāti pāṇḍavān
english: Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, conquered the entire earth. The Sairandhrī has told me of you — for she knows the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃyaccha māmakān aśvāṃs tathaiva tvaṃ bṛhannaḍe kurubhir yotsyamānasya godhanāni parīpsataḥ
english: So take hold of my horses, O Bṛhannaḍā — for me as I am about to fight the Kurus in order to recover the cattle-wealth."

sanskrit: arjunasya kilāsīs tvaṃ sārathir dayitaḥ purā tvayājayat sahāyena pṛthivīṃ pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: "You were indeed formerly the beloved charioteer of Arjuna; with your help as ally, that bull of the Pāṇḍavas conquered the earth.

sanskrit: evam uktā pratyuvāca rājaputraṃ bṛhannaḍā kā śaktir mama sārathyaṃ kartuṃ saṃgrāmamūrdhani
english: Thus addressed, Bṛhannaḍā replied to the prince: "What power have I to serve as charioteer at the head of battle?

sanskrit: gītaṃ vā yadi vā nṛttaṃ vāditraṃ vā pṛthagvidham tat kariṣyāmi bhadraṃ te sārathyaṃ tu kuto mayi
english: Singing, or dancing, or playing various instruments — that I will do; blessings on you — but where would chariot-driving come from in me?"

sanskrit: uttara uvāca bṛhannaḍe gāyano vā nartano vā punar bhava kṣipraṃ me ratham āsthāya nigṛhṇīṣva hayottamān
english: Uttara said: "Be a singer or a dancer again later, O Bṛhannaḍā — for now, quickly mount my chariot and take hold of the excellent horses."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa tatra narmasaṃyuktam akarot pāṇḍavo bahu uttarāyāḥ pramukhataḥ sarvaṃ jānann ariṃdama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There the Pāṇḍava, knowing everything, performed many playful acts right in front of Uttarā, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: ūrdhvam utkṣipya kavacaṃ śarīre pratyamuñcata kumāryas tatra taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāhasan pṛthulocanāḥ
english: He tossed a piece of armor up into the air and then buckled it onto his body; the wide-eyed maidens there, seeing him, laughed aloud.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā vimuhyantaṃ svayam evottaras tataḥ kavacena mahārheṇa samanahyad bṛhannaḍām
english: Seeing him fumbling, Uttara himself then bound on Bṛhannaḍā the most excellent and precious armor.

sanskrit: sa bibhrat kavacaṃ cāgryaṃ svayam apy aṃśumatprabham dhvajaṃ ca siṃham ucchritya sārathye samakalpayat
english: He himself also wore the finest armor, brilliant as rays of light, and raising the lion-banner, prepared himself for the role of charioteer.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi ca mahārhāṇi bāṇāṃś ca rucirān bahūn ādāya prayayau vīraḥ sa bṛhannaḍasārathiḥ
english: Taking up the most precious bows and many beautiful arrows, the hero set out with Bṛhannaḍā as charioteer.

sanskrit: athottarā ca kanyāś ca sakhyas tām abruvaṃs tadā bṛhannaḍe ānayethā vāsāṃsi rucirāṇi naḥ
english: Then Uttarā and the maiden companions said to her: "O Bṛhannaḍā, bring us beautiful garments —

sanskrit: pāñcālikārthaṃ sūkṣmāṇi citrāṇi vividhāni ca vijitya saṃgrāmagatān bhīṣmadroṇamukhān kurūn
english: — fine and variegated and of many kinds, for the sake of our dolls, after defeating in battle the Kurus headed by Bhīṣma and Droṇa."

sanskrit: atha tā bruvatīḥ kanyāḥ sahitāḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ pratyuvāca hasan pārtho meghadundubhiniḥsvanaḥ
english: Then to those maidens speaking together, the son of Pāṇḍu replied with a laugh — Pārtha, whose voice resounded like the drum of a thunder-cloud:

sanskrit: yady uttaro 'yaṃ saṃgrāme vijeṣyati mahārathān athāhariṣye vāsāṃsi divyāni rucirāṇi ca
english: "If this Uttara defeats the great warriors in battle, then I shall bring back divine and beautiful garments for you."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu bībhatsus tataḥ prācodayad dhayān kurūn abhimukhāñ śūro nānādhvajapatākinaḥ
english: Having said this, Bībhatsu the hero then urged on the horses toward the Kurus, who displayed many banners and pennants.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa rājadhānyā niryāya vairāṭiḥ pṛthivīṃjayaḥ prayāhīty abravīt sūtaṃ yatra te kuravo gatāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having departed from the royal capital, Vairāṭi the earth-conqueror said to his charioteer: "Drive on to where the Kurus have gone."

sanskrit: samavetān kurūn yāvaj jigīṣūn avajitya vai gāś caiṣāṃ kṣipram ādāya punar āyāmi svaṃ puram
english: "Having swiftly defeated the assembled Kurus who seek victory, and having quickly recovered their cattle, I shall return to my own city."

sanskrit: tatas tāṃś codayām āsa sadaśvān pāṇḍunandanaḥ te hayā narasiṃhena coditā vātaraṃhasaḥ ālikhanta ivākāśam ūhuḥ kāñcanamālinaḥ
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu urged on the excellent horses. Those steeds, urged on by the lion among men, swift as the wind, seemed to scratch at the sky as they sped forward, wearing their golden garlands.

sanskrit: nātidūram atho yātvā matsyaputradhanaṃjayau avekṣetām amitraghnau kurūṇāṃ balināṃ balam śmaśānam abhito gatvā āsasāda kurūn atha
english: Having gone not too great a distance, the son of Matsya and Dhanaṃjaya — both destroyers of enemies — surveyed the great host of the powerful Kurus. Going toward the cremation ground, they then came upon the Kurus.

sanskrit: tad anīkaṃ mahat teṣāṃ vibabhau sāgarasvanam sarpamāṇam ivākāśe vanaṃ bahulapādapam
english: That great army of theirs blazed forth with the roar of the ocean, seeming to spread across the sky like a forest dense with trees.

sanskrit: dadṛśe pārthivo reṇur janitas tena sarpatā dṛṣṭipraṇāśo bhūtānāṃ divaspṛṅ narasattama
english: The dust raised by that army spreading out was seen — touching the sky, destroying the sight of all beings, O best of men.

sanskrit: tad anīkaṃ mahad dṛṣṭvā gajāśvarathasaṃkulam karṇaduryodhanakṛpair guptaṃ śāṃtanavena ca
english: Seeing that great army crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, guarded by Karṇa, Duryodhana, Kṛpa and the son of Śāntanu,

sanskrit: droṇena ca saputreṇa maheṣvāsena dhīmatā hṛṣṭaromā bhayodvignaḥ pārthaṃ vairāṭir abravīt
english: — and by Droṇa together with his son, that great archer of keen intellect — with hair standing on end and shaken by fear, Vairāṭi spoke to Pārtha:

sanskrit: notsahe kurubhir yoddhuṃ romaharṣaṃ hi paśya me bahupravīram atyugraṃ devair api durāsadam pratiyoddhuṃ na śakṣyāmi kurusainyam anantakam
english: "I do not dare to fight with the Kurus — look at how my hair stands on end! Full of many heroes and utterly terrible, difficult to approach even for the gods, I cannot face the endless Kuru army in battle."

sanskrit: nāśaṃse bhāratīṃ senāṃ praveṣṭuṃ bhīmakārmukām rathanāgāśvakalilāṃ pattidhvajasamākulām dṛṣṭvaiva hi parān ājāv ātmā pravyathatīva me
english: "I have no confidence in entering the Bhārata army with its terrible bows, crowded with chariots, elephants and horses, swarming with foot-soldiers and banners — for merely at the sight of the foe in battle, my own self seems to tremble.

sanskrit: yatra droṇaś ca bhīṣmaś ca kṛpaḥ karṇo viviṃśatiḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca somadatto 'tha bāhlikaḥ
english: Where Droṇa and Bhīṣma are, Kṛpa, Karṇa and Viviṃśati, Aśvatthāmā and Vikarṇa, Somadatta and Bāhlika —

sanskrit: duryodhanas tathā vīro rājā ca rathināṃ varaḥ dyutimanto maheṣvāsāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english: — and also the heroic Duryodhana, that king foremost among chariot-warriors — all of them glorious great archers, all skilled in warfare —

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva hi kurūn etān vyūḍhānīkān prahāriṇaḥ hṛṣitāni ca romāṇi kaśmalaṃ cāgataṃ mama
english: — merely beholding these Kurus arrayed in battle-formation, ready to strike, my hair has bristled and faintness has come upon me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca aviyāto viyātasya maurkhyād dhūrtasya paśyataḥ paridevayate mandaḥ sakāśe savyasācinaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In the very presence of the left-handed archer, this foolish one — through his own stupidity — laments before the knowledgeable one who has ventured what he has not ventured.

sanskrit: trigartān me pitā yātaḥ śūnye saṃpraṇidhāya mām sarvāṃ senām upādāya na me santīha sainikāḥ
english: "My father has gone against the Trigarta king, leaving me behind in an empty city with all the army taken — I have no soldiers here.

sanskrit: so 'ham eko bahūn bālaḥ kṛtāstrān akṛtaśramaḥ pratiyoddhuṃ na śakṣyāmi nivartasva bṛhannaḍe
english: I alone, a mere boy, untrained in effort, cannot face so many skilled warriors in battle. Turn back, O Bṛhannaḍā!"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhayena dīnarūpo 'si dviṣatāṃ harṣavardhanaḥ na ca tāvat kṛtaṃ kiṃ cit paraiḥ karma raṇājire
english: Arjuna said: "You appear wretched with fear, increasing the joy of your enemies — and yet the foes have not yet done any deed on the battlefield.

sanskrit: svayam eva ca mām āttha vaha māṃ kauravān prati so 'haṃ tvāṃ tatra neṣyāmi yatraite bahulā dhvajāḥ
english: And you yourself told me, 'Drive me against the Kauravas.' I shall take you to that very place where all these banners are flying.

sanskrit: madhyam āmiṣagṛdhrāṇāṃ kurūṇām ātatāyinām neṣyāmi tvāṃ mahābāho pṛthivyām api yudhyatām
english: Into the midst of those flesh-greedy, violent Kurus — fighters of the earth — I shall take you, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: tathā strīṣu pratiśrutya pauruṣaṃ puruṣeṣu ca katthamāno 'bhiniryāya kimarthaṃ na yuyutsase
english: Having thus promised valor to the women and boasted of it among men, having marched out — why will you not fight?

sanskrit: na ced vijitya gās tās tvaṃ gṛhān vai pratiyāsyasi prahasiṣyanti vīra tvāṃ narā nāryaś ca saṃgatāḥ
english: If you return home without having won back those cattle, O hero, men and women gathered together will mock you.

sanskrit: aham apy atra sairandhryā stutaḥ sārathyakarmaṇi na hi śakṣyāmy anirjitya gāḥ prayātuṃ puraṃ prati
english: I too was here praised by the Sairandhrī for the task of charioteering — I cannot go back to the city without having won the cattle.

sanskrit: stotreṇa caiva sairandhryās tava vākyena tena ca kathaṃ na yudhyeyam ahaṃ kurūn sarvān sthiro bhava
english: Given the Sairandhrī's praise and your own words to me, how could I not fight all the Kurus? Be steady!"

sanskrit: uttara uvāca kāmaṃ harantu matsyānāṃ bhūyāṃsaṃ kuravo dhanam prahasantu ca māṃ nāryo narā vāpi bṛhannaḍe
english: Uttara said: "Let the Kurus take away the greater part of the Matsya people's wealth if they wish, and let women and men mock me too, O Bṛhannaḍā —

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā prādravad bhīto rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī tyaktvā mānaṃ sa mandātmā visṛjya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having said this, the dull-witted one, wearing his earrings, leaped down from the chariot in terror and ran away, abandoning his pride and casting aside his arrow-laden bow.

sanskrit: bṛhannaḍovāca naiṣa pūrvaiḥ smṛto dharmaḥ kṣatriyasya palāyanam śreyas te maraṇaṃ yuddhe na bhītasya palāyanam
english: Bṛhannaḍā said: "Flight has never been remembered by the ancients as the duty of a Kṣatriya. Death in battle is better for you — not the flight of a coward."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu kaunteyaḥ so 'vaplutya rathottamāt tam anvadhāvad dhāvantaṃ rājaputraṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ dīrghāṃ veṇīṃ vidhunvānaḥ sādhu rakte ca vāsasī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus spoken, the son of Kuntī — Dhanaṃjaya — leaped down from that excellent chariot and chased after the fleeing prince, shaking his long braid and wearing his crimson garments.

sanskrit: vidhūya veṇīṃ dhāvantam ajānanto 'rjunaṃ tadā sainikāḥ prāhasan ke cit tathārūpam avekṣya tam
english: As he ran with his braid flying, certain soldiers who did not recognize Arjuna laughed, seeing him in such a form.

sanskrit: taṃ śīghram abhidhāvantaṃ saṃprekṣya kuravo 'bruvan ka eṣa veṣapracchanno bhasmaneva hutāśanaḥ
english: Seeing him running swiftly, the Kurus said: "Who is this one concealed by his disguise, like fire hidden under ashes?

sanskrit: kiṃ cid asya yathā puṃsaḥ kiṃ cid asya yathā striyaḥ sārūpyam arjunasyeva klībarūpaṃ bibharti ca
english: Something about him is like a man, and something about him is like a woman; yet he bears a resemblance to Arjuna even while wearing an eunuch's guise.

sanskrit: tad evaitac chirogrīvaṃ tau bāhū parighopamau tadvad evāsya vikrāntaṃ nāyam anyo dhanaṃjayāt
english: That very same head and neck, those two arms like iron bars, the same heroic bearing — this one is none other than Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: amareṣv iva devendro mānuṣeṣu dhanaṃjayaḥ ekaḥ ko 'smān upāyāyād anyo loke dhanaṃjayāt
english: As Indra, lord of the gods, is among the immortals — so is Dhanaṃjaya among men. Who else in the world but Dhanaṃjaya would come against us alone?"

sanskrit: ekaḥ putro virāṭasya śūnye saṃnihitaḥ pure sa eṣa kila niryāto bālabhāvān na pauruṣāt
english: "Only one son of Virāṭa, left alone in the empty city — he has indeed marched out, but out of boyish rashness, not out of manly valor.

sanskrit: satreṇa nūnaṃ channaṃ hi carantaṃ pārtham arjunam uttaraḥ sārathiṃ kṛtvā niryāto nagarād bahiḥ
english: Surely Uttara has made Pārtha Arjuna — who was living in disguise — his charioteer and marched out of the city.

sanskrit: sa no manye dhvajān dṛṣṭvā bhīta eṣa palāyati taṃ nūnam eṣa dhāvantaṃ jighṛkṣati dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: It seems to me that he, frightened upon seeing our banners, is fleeing, and Dhanaṃjaya is surely running to catch him as he runs away."

sanskrit: iti sma kuravaḥ sarve vimṛśantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak na ca vyavasituṃ kiṃ cid uttaraṃ śaknuvanti te channaṃ tathā taṃ satreṇa pāṇḍavaṃ prekṣya bhārata
english: Thus all the Kurus reflected separately, each to themselves, and they could not decide anything definite about Uttara, seeing that Pāṇḍava likewise in his disguise, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ tu pradhāvantam anudrutya dhanaṃjayaḥ gatvā padaśataṃ tūrṇaṃ keśapakṣe parāmṛśat
english: But Dhanaṃjaya, pursuing Uttara as he ran headlong, went swiftly a hundred steps and seized him by the hair.
